capturedAtStatement: NULL BY CONSTRUCTION, matching every capture record in this goal.
status: STAGE 0 GATE PASSED — option (c) is WORKABLE, but NOT by the mechanism the frozen plan specified. Both halves of that mechanism were measured and both are wrong.
headline: Keeping the massing in the scene for picking while the far tile draws over it DOES work. It does not work via alpha->0 with allowPicking:false: alpha 0 removes the instance from the pick pass entirely, and allowPicking:false does not remove the tile from the pick pass at all.

harness.discipline: The massing instance is constructed byte-for-byte as CesiumViewport.denseBuildingInstance builds it — same PolygonGeometry, same POSITION_ONLY vertex format, same PerInstanceColorAppearance(flat, translucent), same per-instance colour and show attributes — so the spike tests the shipped construction and not a lookalike.
harness.layout: Six 40 m boxes in one row 120 m apart, camera straight down from 1,500 m (inside the far tier own envelope), alternating far/near roles so hidden subjects and visible controls appear in the SAME frame.
harness.firstAttemptWasInvalid: The first layout used two rows at an oblique pitch and ITS OWN BASELINE FAILED — far:4 picked near:4 before anything was hidden, because the near row occluded the far row. A spike whose control arm is wrong cannot answer anything. The rewrite added an explicit baselineTrustworthy gate, which now reads true (6 of 6 correct).

findings.claim: Per-instance colour alpha 0 REMOVES the instance from the pick pass, exactly like show=false.
findings.evidence: With no tile present at all, alpha 0 returns pickedId null for every far subject; the visible controls in the same frame all pick correctly.
findings.mechanism: Cesium discards translucent fragments below an alpha cutoff, and the discard happens inside czm_non_pick_main() — which the pick fragment shader calls BEFORE writing the pick id — so the fragment never reaches the pick output.

findings.claim: The alpha cutoff is 0.004, and it is sharp.
findings.evidence: Sweep with no tile: alpha 0 FAIL, 0.002 FAIL, 0.004 PASS, 0.01 PASS, 0.02 PASS, 0.05 PASS, 0.1 PASS.
findings.consequence: A massing kept for picking must carry alpha >= 0.004, not 0. At 0.4% opacity the measured tint on the tile is ZERO 8-bit levels on every channel.

findings.claim: allowPicking:false does NOT remove a Primitive from the pick pass. It only clears the pick id, leaving an invisible-id occluder that still writes depth.
findings.evidence: With the opaque tile present, picking fails at EVERY alpha including 0.5 — a plainly visible massing. Removing the tile restores picking at 0.004. The show attribute was read back as [1] in each failing case, so the instance really was shown.
findings.sourceConfirmation: cesium 1.143.0 Build/CesiumUnminified/index.js:48744-48765 — the draw command is pushed into the command list whenever passes.render OR passes.pick, and allowPicking only chooses between colorCommand.pickId = v_pickColor or else leaves it unset.
findings.whyItMatters: The frozen plan treated allowPicking:false as sufficient to keep the tile out of the way of a click. It is not, and no amount of tuning the massing alpha compensates.

escapeRoutes.approach: Hide the far-tier primitives for the DURATION of the scene.pick / drillPick call, then restore.
escapeRoutes.result: WORKS — 3 of 3 far subjects pick correctly, tile visible again immediately after.
escapeRoutes.whyItIsSafe: The pick renders into an offscreen framebuffer; no presented frame is affected, so the toggle cannot be seen. The tile stays OPAQUE, so it self-occludes correctly.

escapeRoutes.approach: Draw the tile in the TRANSLUCENT pass, which does not write depth.
escapeRoutes.caveat: A translucent merged tile cannot self-occlude: buildings behind buildings INSIDE the same tile would show through each other. Measured and recorded, NOT recommended.

contractQuestionsAnswered.q1_invisibleMassingStillReturnsTheRightI: YES, under route D at alpha >= 0.004. 3 of 3 far subjects returned their own id.
contractQuestionsAnswered.q2_noVisualBleedOrZFight: NO BLEED MEASURED. Reading back rendered pixels over each far subject, tile-only and tile-plus-massing are IDENTICAL at [138,107,79] on all three subjects — max channel delta 0. No z-fighting was observed either: the massing is translucent and Cesium translucent state does not write depth, so it cannot fight the opaque tile.
contractQuestionsAnswered.q3_drillPickOrderUnaffected: The tile NEVER appears in a drill result (tileInDrill false everywhere), and every near-tier control subject picks correctly in every arm, so other tiers keep their slots.
contractQuestionsAnswered.q4_frameCost: Not materially worse. Every arm measured FASTER than the all-visible baseline (deltas -0.02 to -0.06 ms/frame at 60 frames), which is expected since a near-zero-alpha instance shades fewer visible pixels. The measurement is a 6-box synthetic scene and is NOT a claim about the citywide primitive.

whatThisDoesNotShow: This is a synthetic 6-box scene, not the citywide dense primitive. It answers a mechanism question, not a performance question at island scale.
No far-tier tile bytes were loaded; the tile stand-in is an opaque Primitive of the same extrusions.
Nothing here is visual acceptance of the far tier.
consequenceForImplementation: The massing hide must write alpha >= 0.004 rather than 0, and must NOT use the show attribute, which is what the shipped comment in CesiumViewport.tsx warns kills picking.
Every scene.pick and scene.drillPick call in the app must bracket the far-tier primitives with show=false/true, or the far tier will silently swallow clicks at far range.
That bracketing is a cross-cutting change to the pick path and is the main design consequence of Stage 0.
